newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian government approves pension reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian government approves pension reform plan.

text.p: Hungarian Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said on Wednesday that the cabinet approved a drastic overhaul of Hungary's pension system, that would be submitted shortly for parliament approval.
Medgyessy said that under the new plan Hungary would retain parts of its antiquated pay-as-you-go system and would also add modern fully funded components.
He also said that generally speaking pension increases in 1998, would be calculated at a rate of average inflation at 13 percent plus three percent, which "means a 16 percent increase."
"This will improve the reliability and safety of our system by modifying the contribution payment," Medgyessy said at a news conference after the government meeting.

Hungary has been under pressure for some time from the World Bank and other international financial agencies to modernise its pension system so that the funds can be invested and grow to help pay pensions for future generations.
Medgyessy said that the new system would "create incentives for payment" because the money would be invested and workers would realise that the money would grow through the investments.
He said the govermnent intended to provide certain guarantees to safeguard the investments.
